scope: Source transit geometry and actual context surfaces, with matching context-only Blender test views. Final browser and composed-scene overlay QA is a separate integration check.

before.method: Every original route vertex plus samples at maximum 3 m centre-line spacing, against the highest actual overlapping render and interactive ground/road/park/wooded/landscape/bridge/station-display triangle. Source triangle coordinates are unchanged. Below-surface or within 5 cm counts as an occlusion/contact risk; a separate count identifies strictly below-surface samples. This measures context occlusion, not tree crowns or building masks.
before.unlitColourIssue: Transitway formerly used a lighter hue for mixed traffic; HML physically coloured bed did not provide a separate continuous service guide.

after.method: Direct check of delivered guide-strip geometry at all guide vertices plus at most 1 m spacing along the centre and both edges; compared with highest actual context triangle across both render and interactive source surfaces. This is stricter than the requested 3 m route sample spacing.
after.caveat: This geometric test covers context surfaces. Buildings and symbolic tree crowns remain ordinary scene geometry; the dedicated cartographic render pass and browser depth override retain guide legibility across them without changing engineering positions.

limitations: The before check samples centres at no more than 3 m; the stricter after check samples actual strip centres and both edges at no more than 1 m. Counts are not identical observation sets.
A clearance below 0.05 m is classified as surface occlusion/contact risk. Negative clearance is separately reported for the before state.
At municipal model edges, a small number of guide samples have no overlapping context triangle; these are excluded from the minimum-clearance claim and counted per route.
Physical meshes and original route physicalPoints remain unchanged. Only the cartographic guide display elevations and widths changed; no geographic reroute occurred.
An 8% cartographic display slope cap and up to 7.779 m guide lift are visualization choices, not new railway engineering or a measured deck height.
Building and symbolic tree-crown occlusion is handled by the explicit cartographic overlay pass or browser depth override, not by raising tracks above buildings.
The source-derived HML second-track gaps and switch connections remain disclosed schematic inferences. This correction does not establish surveyed turnout geometry.
